message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most well‑known titles written by **J.K. Rowling**:

| Series / Title | Publication Year(s) | Notes |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter** (7 books) | 1997–2007 | *Philosopher's Stone* (UK)/*Sorcerer's Stone* (US), *Chamber of Secrets*, *Prisoner of Azkaban*, *Goblet of Fire*, *Order of the Phoenix*, *Half-Blood Prince*, *Deathly Hallows*. These fantasy adventures follow young wizard Harry Potter through Hogwarts School of Witchcraft & Wizardry and his battle against Voldemort. They’ve sold over 500 million copies worldwide and spawned an award‑winning film franchise. |
| **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** (film tie‑in book) | 2018 | A companion guide to the “Fantastic Beasts” movies; it expands on magical creatures introduced in the films. |
| **Quidditch Through the Ages** | 2001 | An encyclopedic look at Quidditch history, rules, and culture—another fan favorite tied into the HP universe. |
| **The Tales of Beedle the Bard** | 2008 | A collection of children’s fairy tales used within the HP world; includes stories such as “The Tale of Three Brothers.” |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel published under her own name. It tackles social issues in a small English town and was adapted into a BBC miniseries. |
| **Cormoran Strike** series (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015–present | A gritty crime‑fiction detective duo featuring private investigator Cormoran Strike and partner Robin Ellacott. Titles include *The Cuckoo’s Calling*, *The Silkworm*, *Career of Evil*, etc., all praised for their realistic dialogue and complex characters. |

These works cover everything from high‑fantasy epics to contemporary mysteries, showcasing Rowling’s versatility beyond the beloved Harry Potter saga.
